title: The robot at the library desk

segments.speaker: Reporter
segments.text: A university library is testing a small robot that answers routine questions near the entrance. Librarian Grace Hall, what problem are you trying to solve?

segments.speaker: Grace
segments.text: At the start of term, staff answer the same location questions hundreds of times: where the printers are, how to find a study room, or which floor contains a collection. The robot can handle those predictable questions while staff deal with requests that need judgment.

segments.speaker: Reporter
segments.text: Does that mean fewer librarians?

segments.speaker: Grace
segments.text: No. The pilot has not reduced staffing. In fact, the robot creates work because someone has to update its information and review questions it fails to answer. The point is to move staff time, not remove staff.

segments.speaker: Reporter
segments.text: Student Amir Khan, how useful is it?

segments.speaker: Amir
segments.text: Good for simple things, but it can sound confident when it has misunderstood you. I asked about borrowing a laptop and it gave me directions to the computer lab. A human would probably have noticed the difference immediately.

segments.speaker: Grace
segments.text: That is exactly the weakness we are measuring. We want the system to admit uncertainty and hand a question to staff sooner instead of guessing.

questions.prompt: What kind of task is the robot mainly designed for?
options: Answering predictable location and service questions
questions.explanationJa: locationやbasic serviceなどroutine question向けです。

questions.prompt: Give two examples of questions the robot may answer.
markscheme: Where printers or study rooms are located.
Which floor contains a collection and/or other basic location information.

questions.prompt: What does Grace say about staffing?
options: The robot has already reduced staff numbers.
The pilot shifts staff time but has not reduced staffing.
Only students now work at the library.
questions.explanationJa: staff削減ではなく、routine taskから時間を移すことが目的です。

questions.prompt: Choose TWO weaknesses or costs mentioned.
options: Information must be updated by people.
The robot can misunderstand a question while sounding confident.
The robot cannot move across the floor.
Students must pay to ask questions.
The library loses all digital records.
questions.explanationJa: human maintenanceとconfident misunderstandingが課題です。

questions.prompt: Grace wants the system to admit ________ rather than guess.
questions.explanationJa: guessする前にuncertaintyを示すべきだと述べます。

options: Routine automation is useful when difficult cases are handed to humans.
Students prefer robots in every situation.
Human judgment is no longer needed.
questions.explanationJa: routine automationとhuman judgmentの役割分担が中心です。

segments.speaker: Host
segments.text: Acoustic engineer Nina Park has been working with a city on a noisy shopping street. Nina, can design really reduce noise without closing the road?

segments.speaker: Nina
segments.text: Yes, although there is no single device that solves everything. We first mapped when and where noise peaked. Delivery vehicles caused sharp early-morning peaks, while traffic created a steady background for most of the day.

segments.speaker: Host
segments.text: What changed after the mapping?

segments.speaker: Nina
segments.text: The city moved delivery times slightly later, replaced a rough road surface on one block and added planted barriers near outdoor seating. None of those changes made the street silent, but together they reduced the moments people described as most disruptive.

segments.speaker: Host
segments.text: Why not simply measure the average number of decibels?

segments.speaker: Nina
segments.text: Because averages can hide experience. A short, very loud event may disturb sleep even if the daily average looks acceptable. We combine sound measurements with residents' reports so the data reflects both physical levels and how noise is experienced.

segments.speaker: Host
segments.text: So the aim is not silence.

segments.speaker: Nina
segments.text: Exactly. Cities are active places. The aim is to reduce avoidable noise and protect quieter periods, not pretend urban life should make no sound.

questions.prompt: What did the team do first?
options: Mapped when and where noise peaked
Built a soundproof wall around the city
questions.explanationJa: 最初にnoiseのtime/location patternをmappingしました。

questions.prompt: Give two changes made after the mapping.
markscheme: Delivery times were moved later and/or a rough road surface was replaced.
Planted barriers were added near outdoor seating.
questions.explanationJa: delivery time、road surface、planted barriersなどです。

questions.prompt: Why can daily averages be misleading?
options: They can hide short but very disruptive loud events.
questions.explanationJa: 短時間のloud eventがaverageでは見えにくくなるためです。

questions.prompt: Choose TWO kinds of evidence Nina says should be combined.
questions.explanationJa: sound measurementとresident reportを組み合わせます。

questions.prompt: The goal is to reduce ________ noise, not eliminate all urban sound.
questions.explanationJa: avoidable noiseを減らすことが目標です。

options: Several modest interventions can improve sound conditions without unrealistic goals.
Only road closures can reduce noise.
questions.explanationJa: 複数の小さなinterventionを組み合わせる現実的な立場です。

title: Should an AI study assistant ever say 'I don't know'?

segments.speaker: Moderator
segments.text: Schools are experimenting with AI study assistants. Teacher Rachel Green, what worries you most?

segments.speaker: Rachel
segments.text: Confidence. A student may trust a fluent answer even when the answer is wrong. In a classroom, uncertainty is normal. I want a tool that can say, 'I am not sure; check your textbook or ask your teacher.'

segments.speaker: Moderator
segments.text: Developer Omar Fields, can systems do that reliably?

segments.speaker: Omar
segments.text: We can design them to show sources and confidence signals, but those signals are imperfect. Another challenge is that students may treat a warning as decoration and still copy the answer. Product design cannot replace teaching students how to verify information.

segments.speaker: Moderator
segments.text: Student Mei Roberts, what do you find useful?

segments.speaker: Mei
segments.text: The best use is when it asks me questions rather than giving me a finished paragraph. If I have to explain why I chose an answer, I notice gaps in my understanding. I use it less for facts and more for practice.

segments.speaker: Rachel
segments.text: That is closer to how I would use it too. The tool should create thinking, not remove it.

segments.speaker: Omar
segments.text: And schools need clear rules about privacy. A useful tutor is not useful enough if students have to upload sensitive personal or assessment data without understanding where it goes.

segments.speaker: Moderator
segments.text: So accuracy matters, but so do verification habits, learning design and privacy.

options: Fluent but wrong answers may appear trustworthy.
questions.explanationJa: fluentな表現が誤答でもtrustworthyに見える点を心配しています。

markscheme: Teach students to verify information rather than relying only on product warnings.
questions.explanationJa: source/confidence表示とverification skillが必要です。

options: Being asked questions that reveal gaps in understanding
questions.explanationJa: answerを与えるよりquestionでthinkingを促す使い方を好みます。

questions.prompt: Choose TWO ideas the panel supports.
options: The tool should encourage thinking rather than remove it.
Privacy rules matter when students upload data.
Students should copy fluent answers directly.
questions.explanationJa: thinkingの促進とprivacyが共通する重要点です。

questions.prompt: Matching task: Match each speaker to their main emphasis: Rachel and Omar.
markscheme: Rachel — misleading confidence / the need for the system to admit uncertainty.
Omar — imperfect confidence signals, verification habits and/or privacy safeguards.
questions.explanationJa: Rachelはconfidence、Omarはsignalの限界・verification・privacyを強調しています。

questions.prompt: What is the moderator's final purpose?
options: To say accuracy is the only issue
To summarize several conditions for responsible use
To argue students should never ask teachers
questions.explanationJa: accuracyだけでなくverification、learning design、privacyをまとめています。
